reason: I'll start with filtering blood to see what enters the kidney's recovery route.
expectation: I expect water and small dissolved substances, including glucose and waste, to pass through while blood cells and large proteins stay in the vessels.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with waste, so I want to follow the recovery step.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube is described as returning useful substances to the blood, so it follows naturally from filtering.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, while some fluid and waste continue onward.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to see recovery first.

effect: Recovery returned useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving urine. I can now build its route to the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense that filtering and taking substances back are separate steps.
reason: The ureters connect the kidney outlets toward the bladder, so I'll add them first.
expectation: I expect the two ureters to attach to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to be added.

alternatives.reason: I could add the bladder first, but I want to follow the route from the kidneys downward.

effect: The ureters now lead from the kidneys toward the bladder position, leaving the bladder to complete the route.
reaction: The muscular squeezes moving fluid along the tubes are a useful detail.
reason: Adding the bladder is the only offered combination and completes the drainage route.
expectation: I expect the bladder to connect to the ureters and collect urine from the kidneys.

effect: The bladder completes the route from the kidneys; urine stays the same fluid as it travels through the ureters.
reaction: The continuous fluid trail made the route easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering useful substances after filtration was most worthwhile: it showed why filtering alone doesn't just remove waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the bladder was straightforward and the only available combination, though it completed the route.

surprise.text: I was interested that glucose and water pass through the filter before useful substances are taken back into the blood.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; the pictures and goals made both recovery and the drainage route clear.

continue.text: I would continue to see how another body system works, though the final fitting was predictable.
